subject.title: [Feature]: Stop Burying Your Agent's Soul: Configurable Context File Elevation

question: Should per-file bootstrap elevation/exclusion be accepted as a core typed config surface, or should OpenClaw first expose this through a documented plugin/context-engine contract?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the durable API changes prompt authority, prompt-cache stability, and the public config/plugin boundary, which needs maintainer product direction.

options.title: Extend plugin/context-engine contract
options.body: Document or add the minimal plugin/context-engine hook needed for external packages to elevate and exclude bootstrap files without adding another core config knob.

options.title: Add narrow core config
options.body: Accept a typed core config for ordered pattern-to-section elevation with explicit exclusion behavior, plus schema, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Keep Project Context flat
options.body: Reject elevation as core behavior for now and direct users to context-engine plugins or manual prompt additions for persona-specific weighting.

recommendation.title: Extend plugin/context-engine contract
recommendation.body: Document or add the minimal plugin/context-engine hook needed for external packages to elevate and exclude bootstrap files without adding another core config knob.

likelyOwner.reason: He has current-line ownership evidence on the affected prompt/config files and already framed the issue as a core config versus plugin/context-engine choice.
